newsitem.title: UK: Halifax up, squeezed on shr buyback hopes.
newsitem.headline: Halifax up, squeezed on shr buyback hopes.

text.p: Halifax Plc shares jumped on Wednesday after a British newspaper quoted the bank's chief executive as saying the board would consider returning capital to shareholders unless it could earn them a better return.
At 0821 GMT, the shares were up 15-1/2p to 776 in active trading.

In an interview with the Guardian, Halifax chief executive Mike Blackburn said the bank was "sitting on a lot of surplus capital" and that "the board is agreed we might be best advised to distribute to shareholders."
"It was taken to mean a share buyback or special dividend, and the market is just getting squeezed," one market maker said of the newspaper report.
A spokeswoman for the building society turned bank said no decision has been made.
"It's one of our options," she said referring to a possible share buyback or special dividend. Blackburn's comments in the newspaper, she said, "weren't taken completely out of context."
She also noted that the Halifax, which floated on the London Stock Exchange on June 20, also could use the cash pile of cash for acquisitions.
Halifax has been widely tipped as a potential bidder for other financial services providers.
A third option for the excess cash of around 3.0 billion pounds ($5 billion) would be to reinvest it, concentrating on organic growth, she said.
